messages:
elaine: heads-up — customer Acme reporting 401 from `go get` in CI when pulling our go sdk. They have a `replace` in their go.mod to a local path and CI fails against proxy.golang.org :sob:
jordan: can you paste the CI log + go.mod snippet? is this on their public repo or private?
elaine: private. ci log shows proxy 401. snippet attached:

```
go: github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2: reading https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/redwood/inference-go/@v/v2.info: 401 Unauthorized
go env GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct
```

and go.mod excerpt:

```
module acme/service

require github.com/redwood/inference-go v2.0.0
replace github.com/redwood/inference-go => ../inference-go-local
```

alex: sounds like the replace points at a local path (../inference-go-local) so `go` is trying to talk to the proxy for the module path but the repo is private — proxy returns 401. common CI trap.
sam: yup. either make the module path resolvable by the CI runner (ssh creds) or tell `go` to skip the proxy for that module via GOPRIVATE. quick check: do they use GOPROXY explicitly in CI?
morgan: customer shared their CI env: GOPROXY is default (https://proxy.golang.org,direct) and no GOPRIVATE. also GONOSUMDB unset.
jordan: immediate workaround for CI (short-term): set env in pipeline:

```
export GOPRIVATE=github.com/redwood
export GONOSUMDB=github.com/redwood
export GOPROXY=direct
```

That forces go to fetch directly and not use sumdb/proxy. also ensure git creds available (SSH key or token).

elaine: noted. they tried GOPRIVATE but still getting 401 because their runner uses HTTPs and no stored credentials. they can't add SSH key easily in our customer's cloud CI.

alex: alternative: publish a tagged module version (v2.0.1) on a public repo or on their private org with proper tags so go proxy can fetch with auth, or vendor the dependency into their repo. but public tag would expose code if it's private — not ideal.

sam: another option: change the replace to point to the ssh URL of the repo instead of local path, e.g. `replace github.com/redwood/inference-go => git@github.com:redwood/inference-go.git v0.0.0-...` but replace doesn't accept git URLs with versions nicely. safest: set pipeline to use `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=1` plus credentials or install a deploy key.

morgan: customer asked if we can change our module path to avoid proxy issues. we shouldn't change upstream module path; that's a breaking change.

ci-bot: :information_source: recommended kb article: https://go.dev/doc/modules/private or https://golang.org/doc/faq#private_modules

jordan: action items:
- propose quick pipeline env change (GOPRIVATE + GOPROXY=direct) + add token/credential to runner (customer).
- longer term: doc blurb in our SDK README about private-repo CI guidance + example pipeline snippets.
- engineering: consider tagging a 2.0.1 release that doesn't require local replace for customers doing adhoc local dev? alex to advise.

alex: I can draft a patch release if we decide it's helpful, but we should avoid changing internal layout. I'll also add a short section in the SDK README explaining GOPRIVATE/GONOSUMDB and CI snippets.

elaine: customer applied the GOPRIVATE+GOPROXY=direct workaround and provided new CI log — fetch succeeded. they added a short PR to their pipeline to inject a personal access token.

sam: great. flagging for docs team and adding internal KB entry for support runbook.

elaine: marking customer unblocked, will follow up with a doc link and keep ticket open for a day to confirm stability. thanks all :thumbsup:
